implication: A Reg. 31(4) filing triggers the requirement that an acquirer disclosing a substantial holding must proceed to open offer (Reg. 38) within 4 weeks unless an exemption applies; partners must verify whether the acquirer is a promoter, white-knight or third party, and whether creeping exemption (5% per quarter) or other carve-outs have been invoked.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Reg. 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure of acquisition of shares crossing 25% threshold or other specified limits; must be filed immediately upon acquisition.
Open offer obligation triggered by Reg. 31(4) filing; acquirer must make public offer to all shareholders unless exemption applies.
Creeping acquisition exemption; acquirer may increase holding by up to 5% per financial year without triggering open offer.
Exemptions from open offer (subsidiary, intra-group transfer, rights issue, bonus shares, stock split); critical to verify applicability.
Nominee director and change of control reporting; disclosure to Registrar of Companies post-acquisition.
Exchange disclosure of material events; acquisition disclosures must be filed on BSE/NSE simultaneously.
Definition of 'acquirer' and 'person acting in concert' (PAC); critical for determining joint acquisition and consolidated disclosure.

headline: Waaree Renewable Technologies discloses substantial acquisition under SEBI takeover regulations
sum: Waaree Renewable Technologies Limited filed a Regulation 31(4) disclosure under the SEBI Takeover Code, signalling a material acquisition of shares or change of control event requiring mandatory public disclosure under Indian securities law.
detail: Waaree Renewable Technologies (formerly Waaree Energies), a renewable energy company listed on NSE, filed a mandatory disclosure of substantial acquisition under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI (SAST) Regulations, 2011. This filing is triggered when an acquirer crosses 25% of voting capital or triggers other thresholds defined in the Code. The disclosure must be followed by either an open offer to public shareholders under Reg. 38 or a valid exemption claim within the prescribed timeline.
